route: Courmayeur → Pavillon du Mont Fréty → Punta Helbronner → Courmayeur
intro:
This morning started a little later than planned, but when I stepped onto the balcony of my hotel in Courmayeur, I was greeted by an absolutely beautiful sight. The air was crisp, just 4°C (39°F), but the skies were clear, and the mountains stood majestically in the distance. It was a wonderful way to begin what would become one of the most memorable days of my journey.

Today’s destination was Skyway Monte Bianco, a remarkable cable car system that climbs high into the Italian Alps, bringing visitors face-to-face with some of the most spectacular mountain scenery in Europe.

I arrived around 11 a.m., having booked a journey all the way to the summit at Punta Helbronner, along with lunch at the intermediate station.

The first cable car ride was absolutely incredible. What makes Skyway so special is that the cabins slowly rotate 360 degrees as they ascend, allowing you to experience the scenery in every direction. As we climbed from approximately 1,300 meters to 2,100 meters, the entire valley began opening beneath us. Mountains rose on every side, their rugged faces becoming more impressive with every passing moment.

I was simply in awe.

The crisp mountain air, the clear skies, and the sheer beauty of everything surrounding me were almost overwhelming. There was something extraordinary about seeing these enormous mountains from such a unique perspective.

Of course, looking straight down was another matter entirely!

As I realized just how high we were climbing, I experienced a little vertigo. The beauty was breathtaking, but so was the height.

When I arrived at Pavillon du Mont Fréty (the Pavilion), the intermediate station of Skyway Monte Bianco, I decided to spend about five to ten minutes getting comfortable with the elevation before continuing.

While there, I explored the museum and discovered something particularly interesting about winemaking in the Alps. They have a vineyard in the valley, but part of their winemaking process involves bringing wine up into the mountains and placing it within the glacier’s icy environment. The idea of using these extreme conditions as part of the winemaking process was fascinating. It was something I certainly hadn’t expected to learn about while visiting Mont Blanc.

Once I felt acclimated, it was time to continue upward to Punta Helbronner.

This second cable car ride was even more spectacular—and a little more intimidating!

Again, the cabin rotated a full 360 degrees, revealing incredible views of the valley, the surrounding mountains, and the increasingly dramatic landscape below. But this section was noticeably steeper.

Each time the cable car passed one of the support towers, there was a sudden sway and a little jolt. For a brief moment, it created that unmistakable feeling of your stomach dropping.

It was enough to make me think, “Uh-oh!”

Still, the views were so extraordinary that I couldn’t stop looking around.

Finally, I reached Punta Helbronner, standing approximately 3,466 meters (11,371 feet) above sea level.

What an incredible place!

I was immediately captivated by Mont Blanc.

Although clouds obscured its summit, the surrounding jagged peaks were absolutely magnificent. There was something almost impossible to describe about the sheer mass of these mountains. Their enormous rocky faces, sharp ridgelines, and snow-covered slopes stretched across the landscape in every direction.

The clouds seemed to move and swirl around the highest peaks, occasionally revealing different portions of the mountain.

Standing there, surrounded by such immense natural beauty, I couldn’t help but feel a sense of amazement.

From the panoramic viewing area, I could also look through openings between the mountains into distant valleys. Far away, I noticed a dam, with additional snowcapped mountains rising beyond it.

Every direction offered something different.

There were towering peaks, deep valleys, enormous rock formations, snow, ice, and clouds drifting across the mountainsides. The scale of everything was simply extraordinary.

It was one of those moments when photographs, no matter how many you take, cannot fully capture what you’re experiencing.

Eventually, it was time to descend to the Pavilion for lunch.

Interestingly, I hadn’t fully appreciated just how steep the cable car route was until we started going down. Looking toward the valley below made the elevation change even more apparent. Each time we passed a support tower, the cabin would sway and create that brief sensation of weightlessness.

It certainly added a little excitement to the descent!

Once back at the Pavilion, I headed to the restaurant for a buffet lunch.

There was quite a selection of food, and I enjoyed ravioli, polenta, cheese with potatoes, and tomato soup with sausage. For dessert, I had a Mont Blanc cake accompanied by a cappuccino.

Everything was delicious and very filling.

But as good as the food was, it wasn’t the highlight of lunch.

That distinction belonged to the view.

I was fortunate enough to get a window seat looking directly toward Mont Blanc and the surrounding mountains.

For approximately an hour and twenty minutes, I sat there enjoying my meal and simply taking in the scenery.

One particular detail captured my attention.

A cloud rested directly over the summit of Mont Blanc, almost like a cap placed gently on top of the mountain. Throughout my entire lunch, it seemed to remain in exactly the same position.

It was fascinating.

I kept looking at that cloud, the mountain beneath it, and the intricate details of the surrounding landscape. The longer I looked, the more I noticed.

The rocky ridges, the snow-covered sections, the valleys stretching far below—every part of the landscape seemed to tell its own story.

There was something incredibly peaceful about sitting there.

No rushing. No worrying about the next destination. Just enjoying a wonderful meal while looking out at one of the most beautiful mountain landscapes I have ever seen.

As I sat there, my thoughts turned to Jehovah’s creation and the remarkable processes that make everything around us possible.

I thought about the water cycle, the formation of clouds, the snow and ice covering the mountains, and the way water eventually makes its journey down into the valleys below.

There is so much happening in creation that we rarely stop to consider.

Yet here I was, sitting high in the Alps, watching some of those processes unfold right before my eyes.

It was a beautiful reminder of the extraordinary wisdom and power behind everything Jehovah has made.

Eventually, it was time to leave.

I boarded the cable car for the final descent into the valley. By now, the afternoon sun was beginning to settle lower in the sky, and shadows were slowly creeping across the mountainsides.

The changing light gave the landscape an entirely different appearance.

Areas that had been brightly illuminated earlier were now falling into shadow, while other sections of the mountains still caught the warmth of the afternoon sunlight.

Naturally, I took more photographs.

I wanted to capture as much as possible, although I knew that no photograph could truly reproduce the feeling of standing among these enormous mountains.

There is something about the mountains that deeply appeals to me.

Perhaps it is their size, their rugged beauty, or the way they make everything else seem so small. Perhaps it is the peacefulness of being surrounded by something so magnificent.

Whatever it is, I find myself drawn to them again and again.

Today was another reminder of why.

As I returned to my hotel in Courmayeur, I couldn’t help but reflect on the time I’ve spent in Italy. I arrived on October 24, and now, after eleven days, it’s almost time to say goodbye to a country that has given me so many wonderful memories.

From wandering through the canals and narrow streets of Venice to standing among the towering peaks of the Dolomites, enjoying the peaceful shores of Lake Garda, exploring the historic streets of Bologna, and experiencing the breathtaking beauty of the Alps, Italy has been an incredible part of this journey.

I’ve experienced beautiful landscapes, delicious food, warm hospitality, and moments that have genuinely taken my breath away. There have been long drives, unexpected challenges, and times when the roads tested my nerves. But looking back, even those experiences have become part of the adventure.

What stands out most is just how much beauty and variety I’ve encountered in such a relatively short time. Every region seemed to offer something different, and around nearly every corner there was another reminder of the incredible beauty of Jehovah’s creation.

Tomorrow, I’ll cross the border into France and begin the next chapter of The Long Way Around.

There’s a little sadness in leaving Italy behind, especially knowing how much I’ve enjoyed my time here. But that’s the wonderful thing about a journey like this. Every goodbye means another adventure is waiting just down the road.

Italy has given me memories I’ll carry long after this trip ends. And while this chapter is coming to a close, the journey is far from over.

There are still new roads to travel, new places to discover, and more postcards waiting to be written.
